issue.title: ast_edit AX: AST validation does not block broken writes, and the schema contradicts the tool's two-step contract

steps: Use ast_edit on src/service.ts with old_string `  ship(id: string): Order {` and new_string `  ship(id: string): Order {{{` and force: true, then check the file with tsc.
expected: ast_edit refuses to write an edit that its AST validation shows introduces a syntax error, leaving src/service.ts unchanged.
defect: ast_edit writes the broken code and reports "Successfully applied edit to: .../src/service.ts" together with "AST validation: FAILED"; tsc then reports `error TS1005: ',' expected`.

fault location.explanation: Only editData.error blocks the write; a failed editData.astValidation is ignored and the edit proceeds to writeEditResult; PR #3058 makes validation authoritative and rejects edits that introduce new syntax errors.
Writes the new content and builds a message that starts with 'Successfully applied edit' even when AST validation is FAILED; PR #3058 no longer writes in that case.
The agent-facing schema describes force as 'Internal execution control. Managed automatically.', contradicting the two-step preview/apply contract; PR #3058 rewrites the description.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/3058. In v0.10.0, ast_edit computes an AST validation of the edited content in calculateEdit, but executeApply only returns early on editData.error; the validation result is merely printed. writeEditResult therefore writes a syntactically broken file to disk and reports 'Successfully applied edit ... AST validation: FAILED'. In addition the schema tells the model that force is 'Internal execution control. Managed automatically.', so callers either believe a preview was applied or always pass force: true and skip the preview. Commit 0efa7c6 (PR #3058, 'make ast_edit validation authoritative') blocks writes whose validation shows newly introduced errors (new validation-categorizer logic, changes in edit-calculator.ts and ast-edit-invocation.ts) and describes the two-step contract in the force parameter. The fix first ships in v0.11.0, the pinned version, so the case is tested at v0.10.0.
